root.claim: A deterministic fixed-tape machine multiplies two $n$-bit integers exactly in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time, with $\kappa=2^{-182}$, below the $n\lg n$ conjecture in this model.
root.method: bound the cost of an exact multiplication whose transform layers are made cheap by two tape procedures, then fix parameters so every cost term fits

motivation.text: Each transform level scans $\Theta(n)$ stored bits, so the transform layers alone cost $\Theta(n\log n)$; the savings must come from both address movement and arithmetic.

quote.quote: Scanning an array of Θ(n) stored bits at each of Θ(log n) transform levels already costs Θ(n log n). We therefore need savings in both movement and arithmetic.

root.salient: the logarithmic factor is reduced by a power, $(\lg n)^{1-\kappa}$, so the bound is strictly below $n\lg n$ through all input lengths

adds.name: stored bit volume
adds.meaning: the number of stored data bits in the array on which a procedure runs.

adds.name: saving exponent
adds.meaning: the fixed exponent $\kappa=2^{-182}$ by which the logarithmic factor is reduced.

adds.name: field width
adds.meaning: the number of bits in each of the two address fields that an interchange swaps.

adds.name: interchange exponent
adds.meaning: a fixed exponent $\tau<1$ bounding the interchange cost as a power of the field width.

adds.name: chunk count
adds.meaning: the number of equal-width address chunks in which the same bit position is selected.

adds.name: layer exponent
adds.meaning: a fixed exponent $\lambda'<1$ bounding the butterfly-layer cost as a power of the chunk count.

children.method: realize the tensor product of the two-point kernel by an exact complex phase network with dyadic frame changes, then convert it to the normalized $H_0$ layer

motivation.text: Splitting complete rows among the network's wire roles reduces the volume of each recursive call, so the layer is applied in one pass rather than one axis at a time.

children.claim: The exact product of two $n$-bit integers is obtained from the convolution of their radix-digit coefficients, computed by transforms on a fixed tape layout and then recovered and carried.
children.method: reduce the convolution by a Chinese-remainder map, Gaussian resampling, Bluestein's identity and a phase twist to a convolution over a polynomial ring, then recover coefficients and propagate carries

motivation.text: Gaussian resampling connects the pairwise-coprime transform lengths of the product to the power-of-two lengths of the synthetic transforms, so the reduction chains these steps.
